content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-GPU-MEM-7123 for cluster-gpu-shared-1 pool: thin-pool-3. Severity: P1. Symptoms: sustained CUDA OOMs and allocator failures. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-oom|gpu-oom-runbook>. Logs attached in thread.
pagerduty: Alert details: triggered at 2026-03-14T09:07:56Z, alert key=CUDA_OOM, current_acks=0. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> eng-sre.
jamie: acked. I'm on it. Seeing a spike in cuda_alloc_retry errors and repeated "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" on nodes: gpu-12,gpu-14,gpu-19. Will collect logs and check autoscaler.
sam: grabbing kv-cache eviction metrics now. On initial glance, the thinpool has lots of fragmentation and frequent eviction churn. Could be KVCACHE + long-lived sessions + high batch request mix.
jamie: stack trace snippet from gpu-14 (recent):
```
2026-03-14T09:06:22Z host=gpu-14 redwood-infer[pid=1421]: runtime error: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at allocate.cu:423
call stack:
  Redwood::CudaAllocator::alloc (+0x1f3)
  Redwood::KVCache::reserve (+0x4b)
  Redwood::RequestHandler::prepare (+0x72)
```

tanya: :eyes: Also seeing large batches from model 'redwood-xl-8k-quant' with seq_len spikes to 6k tokens. That's hitting memory hard. Suggest quickly diverting large-batch traffic to a lower-memory model or throttling.
liam: Can we identify customers impacted? Jay, can you run a short query to map recent requests hitting gpu-14/gpu-19 to customer tokens? Need to estimate customer-facing error rate.
jamie: quick query results: affected requests in last 10m: 342 requests, ~18 unique api_keys. Top 3 customers by error count: cust-fin-42 (120 errs), cust-chat-7 (78 errs), cust-data-9 (42 errs). Errors are 503/INTERNAL with message "allocator failure: out of memory".
pagerduty: Incident assigned to jamie (oncall). Current status: acknowledged. If not resolved within 15m, escalate to eng-sre.
sam: workaround plan: 1) Evict low-priority pods on gpu-14/gpu-19 (preemptible jobs) 2) Taint/cordon and restart redwood-infer daemon on those nodes (rolling) 3) Apply temporary batching throttle for the pool via feature-flag. I'm preparing commands.
jamie: running eviction now: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-14 | grep preemptible | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r kubectl delete pod -n inference`
ops-bot: Deletion jobs queued: 8 pods scheduled for termination on gpu-14. Estimated reclaim: ~9.2Gi each.
jamie: starting cordon on gpu-19, then restarting daemonset: `kubectl cordon gpu-19 && kubectl rollout restart ds/redwood-infer -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-19`
(2m later)
sam: after evictions + restart, memory freed on gpu-14: reclaimed ~72Gi, OOM logs dropped sharply. Monitoring for new allocation failures.
jamie: traffic throttle: toggled feature flag `batch_max_tokens` for pool thin-pool-3 from 8192 -> 2048. Applied via console; config pushed to all routers.
tanya: also flipping model fallback for large requests: requests > 4096 tokens now route to 'redwood-xl-4k-quant' until further notice.
liam: customers notified? Ops already sent proactive note to top 3 impacted customers via status page update and direct emails. Full customer impact: intermittent errors for ~2-4 minutes for the affected customers, now largely mitigated.
pagerduty: Escalation canceled (acked and assigned). Keep monitoring for 30m post-fix.
jamie: monitoring graphs: kernel alloc failure rate went from 14/s -> 0.6/s within 3 minutes. Latency spike normalized.
sam: root cause hypothesis: thinpool fragmentation + a recent spike in large-batch traffic + quantized model memory footprint regressing after last deploy. Will open an infra ticket to investigate KVCACHE fragmentation and GC heuristics.
jamie: temporary fix checklist completed at 2026-03-14T09:22:50Z. Actions remaining: 1) follow-up crashdump analysis (sam) 2) telemetry comparison pre/post deploy (tanya) 3) postmortem doc and timeline (jamie) 4) longer-term: autoscaler tuning and eviction thresholds (liam).
ops-bot: PagerDuty note appended: "workaround applied: evicted preemptible pods, restarted infer ds on gpu-14/19, throttled batch_max_tokens, fallback routing enabled".
jamie: handing off to sam for deeper analysis — I'll stay available for questions.
sam: taking over. Will file PD-incident ticket and link crashdumps. Expected ETA for full RCA: 72 hours.
jamie: thanks all. Closing chat thread for live mitigation. We'll use #postmortems once draft is ready.
